canonical_goal.outcome_variable: o_1=(K,Psi,E) in O_P, where K is a set of real rapidity pairs (k_1,k_2), Psi maps each (k_1,k_2) in K to a two-body wavefunction Psi_{k_1,k_2}(x_1,x_2), and E maps each (k_1,k_2) in K to an energy E_{k_1,k_2}
canonical_goal.target_object: An exact construction of the real-rapidity, two-monomer, point-inversion-odd eigenstates and eigenenergies of two identical one-dimensional bosons of mass m on a ring of circumference L with Hamiltonian H=-(hbar^2/(2m))d^2/dx_1^2-(hbar^2/(2m))d^2/dx_2^2+g delta(x_1-x_2)+g_B delta(x_1)+g_B delta(x_2), for m>0, L>0, hbar>0, g>0, and g_B>0, restricted to wavefunctions satisfying bosonic exchange symmetry Psi(x_2,x_1)=Psi(x_1,x_2), coordinate periodicity Psi(x_1+L,x_2)=Psi(x_1,x_2) and Psi(x_1,x_2+L)=Psi(x_1,x_2), point-inversion oddness Psi(-x_1,-x_2)=-Psi(x_1,x_2), and real rapidity ordering 0<k_1<k_2.
feasibility_constraints: The parameters in the Hamiltonian H=-(hbar^2/(2m))d^2/dx_1^2-(hbar^2/(2m))d^2/dx_2^2+g delta(x_1-x_2)+g_B delta(x_1)+g_B delta(x_2) satisfy m>0, L>0, hbar>0, g>0, and g_B>0; define the reduced mass mu=m/2, the particle-particle scattering length a=-hbar^2/(mu g), and the particle-barrier scattering length a_B=-hbar^2/(m g_B).

The coordinate space is [-L/2,L/2]^2 with opposite edges identified, so admissible wavefunctions obey Psi(x_1+L,x_2)=Psi(x_1,x_2) and Psi(x_1,x_2+L)=Psi(x_1,x_2); inside each connected open component of the complement of x_1=x_2, x_1=0, and x_2=0, Psi is twice differentiable.
Away from x_1=x_2, x_1=0, and x_2=0, every admissible eigenfunction satisfies (-(hbar^2/(2m))d^2/dx_1^2-(hbar^2/(2m))d^2/dx_2^2)Psi_{k_1,k_2}=E_{k_1,k_2}Psi_{k_1,k_2}.

Across the contact hyperplane x_1=x_2, Psi is continuous and, with a=-hbar^2/(mu g) and mu=m/2, the relative-coordinate derivative obeys lim_{r->0+} d_r Psi(X+r/2,X-r/2)-lim_{r->0-} d_r Psi(X+r/2,X-r/2)=-(1/a)Psi(X,X).

Across the barrier hyperplane x_j=0 for each j in {1,2}, Psi is continuous and, with a_B=-hbar^2/(m g_B), obeys lim_{x_j->0+} d_{x_j}Psi-lim_{x_j->0-} d_{x_j}Psi=-(1/a_B)Psi evaluated at x_j=0 while the other coordinate is fixed.
Every admissible eigenfunction is bosonic, Psi_{k_1,k_2}(x_2,x_1)=Psi_{k_1,k_2}(x_1,x_2), and point-inversion odd, Psi_{k_1,k_2}(-x_1,-x_2)=-Psi_{k_1,k_2}(x_1,x_2).

In every open coordinate sector, Psi_{k_1,k_2} is a finite superposition of the eight plane waves exp(i(lambda_{1,i}x_1+lambda_{2,i}x_2)) whose wavevectors are (k_1,k_2), (k_2,k_1), (-k_1,k_2), (-k_2,k_1), (k_1,-k_2), (k_2,-k_1), (-k_1,-k_2), and (-k_2,-k_1), with real rapidities ordered by 0<k_1<k_2.

source_span.verbatim: We assume both constants be positive: g > 0, gB > 0. ... In this paper, we present an exact solution for two one-dimensional δ-interacting bosons subject to periodic boundary conditions in the presence of a δ-function barrier, within the sector of the system’s Hilbert space that is odd under point inversion about the barrier. Both the particle-particle interaction and the particle-barrier interaction are repulsive.

hinted_superfamily.definition: A larger family would include at least one of the following changes: attractive particle-particle coupling g<0, attractive barrier coupling g_B<0, complex rapidity solutions instead of real rapidity pairs 0<k_1<k_2, or the point-inversion-even sector satisfying Psi(-x_1,-x_2)=+Psi(x_1,x_2); these regimes are not part of the completed exact real-rapidity odd-sector construction for repulsive g and g_B.

source_span.verbatim: This article focuses exclusively on the case of repulsive interactions and a repulsive barrier. ... States with complex rapidities (strings) under periodic boundary conditions remain a subject for future investigation. Real rapidity states for attractive interactions and/or an attractive barrier are also of interest...

Exactness means that the constructed wavefunction satisfies periodicity Psi(x_1+L,x_2)=Psi(x_1,x_2) and Psi(x_1,x_2+L)=Psi(x_1,x_2), bosonic exchange symmetry Psi(x_2,x_1)=Psi(x_1,x_2), point-inversion oddness Psi(-x_1,-x_2)=-Psi(x_1,x_2), the free Schrödinger equation away from x_1=x_2, x_1=0, and x_2=0, continuity across x_1=x_2, x_1=0, and x_2=0, the contact jump condition lim_{r->0+} d_r Psi(X+r/2,X-r/2)-lim_{r->0-} d_r Psi(X+r/2,X-r/2)=-(1/a)Psi(X,X), and the barrier jump conditions lim_{x_j->0+} d_{x_j}Psi-lim_{x_j->0-} d_{x_j}Psi=-(1/a_B)Psi at x_j=0 for j in {1,2}.

canonical_goal.target_object: An instrumental large-xi diagnostic proposition derived from the exact odd-sector solution for the point-inversion-odd two-boson ring Hamiltonian H=-(hbar^2/(2m))d^2/dx_1^2-(hbar^2/(2m))d^2/dx_2^2+g delta(x_1-x_2)+g_B delta(x_1)+g_B delta(x_2), with xi=g/(hbar^2/(mL))->+infinity and fixed xi_B=g_B/(hbar^2/(mL))>0: the energy equals (hbar^2/(mL^2))(epsilon(eta_1,eta_2)+epsilon(eta_2,eta_1)+O(xi^{-3})) with epsilon explicitly specified through powers xi^0, xi^{-1}, and xi^{-2}; the xi^{-1} coefficient equals the first-order correction produced by the bilinear form V=tilde_g left_d_{x_1-x_2} delta(x_1-x_2) right_d_{x_1-x_2}, tilde_g=-hbar^4/(mu^2 g), mu=m/2; and the positive xi^{-2} coefficient for eta_1>0, eta_2>0, eta_1!=eta_2, xi_B>0 rules out interpreting V as an ordinary non-degenerate Hermitian perturbing potential beyond first order.
feasibility_constraints: The base Hamiltonian is H=-(hbar^2/(2m))d^2/dx_1^2-(hbar^2/(2m))d^2/dx_2^2+g delta(x_1-x_2)+g_B delta(x_1)+g_B delta(x_2) on a ring of circumference L, with m>0, L>0, hbar>0, g>0, g_B>0, coordinate periodicity, bosonic exchange symmetry, and point-inversion oddness Psi(-x_1,-x_2)=-Psi(x_1,x_2).
Dimensionless couplings are xi=g/(hbar^2/(mL)) and xi_B=g_B/(hbar^2/(mL)); the expansion regime is xi->+infinity with xi_B fixed and positive.

The quantities eta_1 and eta_2 are distinct positive dimensionless one-body rapidities eta_i=L sqrt(2m epsilon_i/hbar^2), where epsilon_i is an eigenvalue with eigenfunction phi_i of -hbar^2 phi_i''(x)/(2m)+g_B delta(x)phi_i(x)=epsilon_i phi_i(x) under one-body periodicity phi_i(x+L)=phi_i(x).

The bilinear object V=tilde_g left_d_{x_1-x_2} delta(x_1-x_2) right_d_{x_1-x_2}, with tilde_g=-hbar^4/(mu^2 g) and mu=m/2, is evaluated only through the equality of its first-order energy correction with the xi^{-1} coefficient of the exact expansion.

source_span.verbatim: The Asymmetric Bethe Ansatz 1/g expansion is E(k1,k2)=...+O(1/xi^3) ... In (18), the 1/g term is identical to the one that can be obtained applying the first order perturbation theory to (17). However notice that for repulsive particle-particle and particle-barrier interactions, the 1/g^2 correction to energy ... is positive...

evidence_channels.formalisation: Let H=-(hbar^2/(2m))d^2/dx_1^2-(hbar^2/(2m))d^2/dx_2^2+g delta(x_1-x_2)+g_B delta(x_1)+g_B delta(x_2) and H_aux=H+g delta(x_1+x_2). If Psi is a periodic bosonic eigenfunction of H_aux and Psi(-x_2,-x_1)=-Psi(x_1,x_2), then at x_1+x_2=0 one has Psi(x_1,x_2)=Psi(x_1,-x_1)=-Psi(x_1,-x_1), hence Psi(x_1,-x_1)=0 and g delta(x_1+x_2)Psi=0 as a distributional multiplication term. Therefore H Psi=H_aux Psi=E Psi. The constructive ansatz for such Psi is a finite superposition of exp(i(lambda_1 x_1+lambda_2 x_2)) over the eight wavevectors (k_1,k_2), (k_2,k_1), (-k_1,k_2), (-k_2,k_1), (k_1,-k_2), (k_2,-k_1), (-k_1,-k_2), and (-k_2,-k_1), constrained by periodicity, exchange symmetry, point-inversion oddness, continuity, and the delta jump conditions.

source_span.paragraph_or_line: Abstract first paragraph; Section 2 opening paragraph
source_span.verbatim: In this article, we apply the recently proposed Asymmetric Bethe Ansatz method to the problem of two one-dimensional, short-range-interacting bosons on a ring in the presence of a δ-function barrier. ... Our goal is to find the eigenstates and eigenenergies of two mass m δ-interacting bosons ... on a ring of a circumference L ... subject to the field of a δ-barrier. We are focussing on the part of the Hilbert space spanned by the states that are odd with respect to the point inversion about the barrier.

stated_goal.formalisation: The stated completed end-state is an exact construction of eigenpairs (Psi_{k_1,k_2},E_{k_1,k_2}) for H=-(hbar^2/(2m))d^2/dx_1^2-(hbar^2/(2m))d^2/dx_2^2+g delta(x_1-x_2)+g_B delta(x_1)+g_B delta(x_2), with m>0, L>0, hbar>0, g>0, g_B>0, periodicity Psi(x_1+L,x_2)=Psi(x_1,x_2) and Psi(x_1,x_2+L)=Psi(x_1,x_2), bosonic exchange symmetry Psi(x_2,x_1)=Psi(x_1,x_2), point-inversion oddness Psi(-x_1,-x_2)=-Psi(x_1,x_2), and real rapidity ordering 0<k_1<k_2. For fixed m>0, L>0, hbar>0, g>0, g_B>0, define mu=m/2, a=-hbar^2/(mu g), and a_B=-hbar^2/(m g_B). The real rapidities satisfy 0<k_1<k_2 and the two equations cos(k_1 L/2)((k_2^2 a a_B - 2) sin(k_2 L/2) + k_2(a+2a_B) cos(k_2 L/2)) + k_1 a sin(k_1 L/2)(k_2 a_B cos(k_2 L/2) - sin(k_2 L/2)) = 0, and k_1^2 a sin(k_1 L/2) sin(k_2 L/2) + 2 k_1 sin(k_2 L/2) cos(k_1 L/2) - k_2^2 a sin(k_1 L/2) sin(k_2 L/2) - 2 k_2 sin(k_1 L/2) cos(k_2 L/2) = 0. The associated energy is E_{k_1,k_2}=(hbar^2/(2m))(k_1^2+k_2^2). The stated application is the following large-repulsion benchmark proposition: Set xi=g/(hbar^2/(mL)) and xi_B=g_B/(hbar^2/(mL))>0. Let eta_i=L sqrt(2m epsilon_i/hbar^2), where epsilon_i has a one-body periodic eigenfunction phi_i satisfying -hbar^2 phi_i''(x)/(2m)+g_B delta(x)phi_i(x)=epsilon_i phi_i(x) and phi_i(x+L)=phi_i(x). For distinct positive eta_1,eta_2, E_asymp=(hbar^2/(mL^2))(epsilon(eta_1,eta_2)+epsilon(eta_2,eta_1)+R_3(xi)), with |R_3(xi)|<=C xi^{-3} for some C>0 and all sufficiently large xi, and epsilon(eta_I,eta_II)=0.5 eta_I^2 - [2 eta_I^2(eta_I^2+xi_B^2)/(eta_I^2+xi_B(2+xi_B))] xi^{-1} + [2 eta_I^2(eta_I^2+xi_B^2)(eta_I^4(eta_II^2+3xi_B)+xi_B^2(2+xi_B)(3xi_B^2+eta_II^2(2+xi_B))+2eta_I^2 xi_B(eta_II^2(2+xi_B)+xi_B(5+3xi_B)))/(xi_B(eta_I^2+xi_B(2+xi_B))^3)] xi^{-2}. The xi^{-1} coefficient is identified with the first-order correction from V=tilde_g left_d_{x_1-x_2} delta(x_1-x_2) right_d_{x_1-x_2}, tilde_g=-hbar^4/(mu^2 g), mu=m/2; the xi^{-2} coefficient is positive for eta_1>0, eta_2>0, eta_1!=eta_2, xi_B>0, so V is not formalised as an ordinary Hermitian perturbing potential beyond first order.

inference_basis: The title, abstract, Section 2, Section 4, and Section 6 prioritise exact eigenstates, exact eigenenergies, rapidity equations, and explicit wavefunctions for the point-inversion-odd sector with repulsive particle-particle and particle-barrier couplings.

Section 3 supplies a method claim: introduce an auxiliary Hamiltonian with an added g delta(x_1+x_2) term and retain states odd under x_1=-x_2 so the auxiliary and physical Hamiltonians share those states.
Section 4 supplies the operational artefacts for the primary goal: two implicit rapidity equations, the energy formula, and explicit six-sector wavefunction formulae.

Section 5 supplies a distinct but derived target proposition: a large-xi expansion through order xi^{-2}, equality of the xi^{-1} term with the derivative-delta first-order correction, and positivity of the xi^{-2} term as evidence that the derivative-delta object is not an ordinary perturbing potential beyond first order.

Section 6 assigns the point-inversion-even sector, quantum-chaos study, complex rapidities, attractive couplings, and the delta-well/non-interacting-spectrum observation to broader or future work rather than to the completed operational goals.

excluded_aims.verbatim: When the barrier strength is a_B=-a/2 (i.e., g_B=-g), the Bethe Ansatz equations reveal that the energy spectrum matches that of a non-interacting, barrier-free system. However, the ground state and likely other eigenstates retain discontinuities induced by delta interactions; the explanation is left for future research.

source_span.verbatim: When the barrier strength is aB = -a/2 (i.e., gB = -g ), the Bethe Ansatz equations reveal that the energy spectrum matches that of a non-interacting, barrier-free system. However, the ground state (and likely other eigenstates) can be shown to retain the characteristic discontinuities induced by δ-interactions. We currently lack an explanation for this phenomenon, which awaits further exploration in future research.

paper_goal.consistency_relation_derivation: The stated, operational, and implicit channels agree on the central achieved end-state: exact real-rapidity eigenstates and eigenenergies for the repulsive, point-inversion-odd two-boson ring Hamiltonian with a delta barrier. The second canonical block is marked instrumental because the abstract presents benchmarking the 1/g expansion as an application of the exact solution, and Section 5 derives an asymptotic diagnostic from that solution rather than defining a separate physical system to solve. The relation is not simply aligned because the abstract and conclusion also contain material framing about method accessibility, non-integrability of the complementary sector, future quantum-chaos studies, attractive-coupling regimes, complex rapidities, and an unexplained delta-well observation; those spans are represented as a methodological claim or excluded future/application material rather than completed canonical outcomes.
